en.name: Our Lady of Kibeho
en.summary: 1981 apparitions to several Rwandan schoolgirls, including visions later interpreted as foreshadowing the 1994 genocide, the first Vatican-approved Marian apparition in Africa.
en.body: Beginning in November 1981, a group of teenage girls at a Catholic secondary school in Kibeho, Rwanda, reported a series of apparitions of the Virgin Mary, who identified herself as Nyina wa Jambo, Mother of the Word, and delivered messages calling for prayer, penance, and conversion amid growing ethnic tension between the country's Hutu and Tutsi populations. Some of the visionaries later reported deeply disturbing visions of rivers of blood, mass killing, and abandoned bodies, images that, following the horrific 1994 Rwandan genocide in which roughly 800,000 people were killed within a hundred days, many came to regard as a prophetic warning that had gone unheeded. Several of the visionaries and their families were themselves killed during the genocide. After an extensive investigation, the local bishop formally approved the apparitions in 2001, and Kibeho became the first Vatican-recognized site of Marian apparitions on the African continent.
